issue.description:
Two false positives of generic-api-key block every commit and every agent Stop in /home/coding/commitgraph (commits there blocked since the hooks were installed 2026-09-28; 13 tracked files uncommitted as of 2026-10-02).

Both are in bead text inside .beads/checkpoint/forensic.jsonl (bead commitgr-6dfbd2ef), verified without printing values: no opaque token of 32+ chars on either flagged line.
1. Scheme colon: keyword 'token', then within 32 bytes the ':' of 'https:' inside 'auths["https://index.docker.io/v1/"]'. The rule takes ':' as the operator and '//index.docker.io/v1/' as the value (21 bytes, alpha+digit, entropy 3.54).
2. Prose comma: keyword 'token', then '... works (tags/list, <image>/0.9.4'. The ',' inside a parenthetical is taken as the operator and an image name plus semver as the value (15 bytes, entropy 3.64).

Fix (src/detector.rs detect_generic_assignment), narrow so no existing true positive is lost:
- A value beginning with '//' is the remainder of a URL, not a credential: skip.
- ',' counts as an operator only in the tuple form (keyword, optional identifier suffix, optional quote, comma), i.e. when the bytes between keyword and comma are identifier, quote or whitespace bytes. Parentheses, slashes or other punctuation in between mean prose.

Acceptance: unit tests for both shapes (synthetic text built at runtime) pass, the existing detector tests still pass, 'secret = <synthetic>' and a quoted tuple still detect, cargo fmt/clippy/test clean, research/rule-coverage.md updated, version bumped, installed binary reports 0 findings for commitgraph --worktree.
issue.title: generic-api-key false positives: URL scheme colon and prose comma treated as assignment operators

issue.description:
Since commitgraph's bead checkpoint was switched to sharded mode on 2026-10-03 (to bring every file under the 10 MB limit), its checkpoint objects are new files, so the worktree scan and the commit gate read them whole instead of only added lines. That surfaced 7 findings in old bead prose (6 generic-api-key, 1 authorization-header). Each was checked by shape without displaying the value; none is a credential.

Shapes seen (a = lowercase letter, A = uppercase, 9 = digit):
1. A host-port-option fragment, 9999/aaaaaaa=aaaaaaa, after the word secret in a sentence about pgbouncer.
2. A hyphenated resource name, aaaaaaaaa-a9-aaaaaaaaaaa, after the word credential (three copies of the same text).
3. aaaaaaaa-9999aa9a after the word credential.
4. Two file paths after the words secret and Secret.
5. A MIME type after the word token.
6. A 32-character mixed-case OAuth client ID after the word token, in closed commitgraph bead commitgr-7e959d96. Client IDs are public identifiers, and that bead holds no client secret.
7. An Authorization match whose value is a single capitalized word, and another whose value is a camelCase function call.

Likely causes. First, the keyword matches across a JSON-escaped newline or a markdown list marker, so the value is taken from the following line. Second, values made only of lowercase words joined by hyphens, slashes, dots or equals signs pass the entropy gate. Third, authorization-header accepts a single word or a call expression as a credential.

Effect: commits in commitgraph are blocked by the PreToolUse gate, and the Stop hook fires every turn there. Bead stores cannot use the inline allow comment, because their files are generated and hand-editing .beads is prohibited. Writing this bead the first time reproduced the bug: its own description tripped generic-api-key in this repo's checkpoint, and the store was rolled back one generation to remove it (backup at /home/coding/scratch/fss-beads-backup-20261003).

Acceptance: unit tests, built at runtime, for each shape above (keyword and value separated by an escaped newline, lowercase hyphenated or path values, single-word and call-expression Authorization values) do not flag, and the existing true-positive tests still pass. secret-scanner --worktree in /home/coding/commitgraph reports 0 findings. The installed binary and the Forgejo pin are updated per this repo's release procedure.
issue.notes: Same bug class, seen independently in bead-rs on 2026-10-03: bead beadrs-1c110ec3 (written by another session, kept on purpose as a live reproduction) is flagged by generic-api-key at forensic.jsonl line 46 of the bead-rs checkpoint. Its root-cause note: the rule takes the word secrets, then a backtick and colon, then a snake_case counter name with an equals sign and a digit, as keyword and value. Fixing this rule unblocks commits in bead-rs as well as commitgraph; both repos' agents are blocked at the commit gate until then.
